QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_68

question.text: Withholding tax on non-resident payments is deducted:

answer.text: By the AIF at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier, at rates in force or applicable DTAA rates

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook (p. 255), the Investment Fund or AIF is required to withhold tax on non-business income payable to non-resident investors at the rates in force or the applicable DTAA rate, at the time of credit of such income to the account of the payee or at the time of payment, whichever is earlier. The Trap: The withholding responsibility lies with the AIF as the deductor, not the individual investor and not SEBI. Non-resident investors are not exempt from withholding on Investment Fund distributions of non-business income. Note: The earlier of credit or payment is the controlling trigger, and the applicable rate is either the rate in force under the Income Tax Act or the DTAA rate, as stated on p. 255 of the source.
